historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 9.3% diverges >30% from EPS 5yr CAGR 15.1%. Book value is depressed by special dividends ($10/share FY2021, $15/share FY2024 ~ $6.7bn) and is not a usable growth anchor; revenue (3yr 6.6%, 5yr 10.5% incl. the COVID/inflation surge) is used instead.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series is reported FCF less SBC and equity-award taxes (interest income not stripped in the CAGR series because it is only split out from FY2023; stripping it in FY2025 alone would distort the rate). FY2022 owner FCF (2,414) is a trough from the inflation-era inventory build, which inflates the 3yr CAGR; the 5yr owner-FCF CAGR (FY2020 5,102 -> FY2025 6,584, 5.2%) tracks reported FCF (5.3%), so SBC is not growing faster than cash flow. Revenue compounded faster than FCF over 5 years because capex rose from 1.7% to 2.0% of revenue (warehouse openings, depots, e-commerce fulfilment).

scenario_narratives.base: Costco keeps compounding the way it has since FY2022: ~25-30 net new warehouses a year (roughly a third outside the US), mid-single-digit comparable sales ex-gasoline, and e-commerce growing in the high teens, so revenue grows 7-7.5% for two years and fades to 4% by FY2036. Membership fee income (the Sep-2024 US/Canada increase fully annualised, renewal rates ~90% in US/Canada, executive-member mix rising) lifts pre-SBC EBITDA margin from ~5.0% to 5.4%, while merchandise gross margin is deliberately reinvested in price. Capex stays elevated near 2.2% of revenue while the opening cadence holds, then fades to 1.5%. This is a superb business priced as one: the base case still lands well below the market because the market capitalises Costco at ~45x earnings.
scenario_narratives.bull: International and digital accelerate: China, Japan, Korea, Sweden/Spain/France openings and new-country entries push unit growth toward 35-40 a year, retail media and Costco Next/ancillary services scale, and a further membership fee increase around FY2029-30 lands without denting renewal. Revenue grows 9% for two years and still 5.5% in FY2036; EBITDA margin reaches 5.9% as fee income and high-margin ancillaries outgrow merchandise. Negative working capital releases more cash as growth stays high. The market's 45x P/E needs roughly this path plus a perpetual premium exit multiple.
scenario_narratives.bear: Growth normalises to low-to-mid single digits as US warehouse density saturates, gasoline and inflation tailwinds reverse, and e-commerce convenience (Amazon same-day grocery, Walmart+/Sam's Club at a ~$50 fee) erodes the trip frequency the membership model depends on. Tariffs and wage pressure are absorbed in price to protect the value proposition, so EBITDA margin drifts down to 4.7%; renewal rates slip as younger digital-first members churn. Costco remains highly profitable and cash-generative (no solvency axis at all); the bear is a de-rating of a normal-growth retailer to a normal multiple.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Costco is valued as an owner would: SBC and the tax cash spent net-settling equity awards are real costs, interest earned on the $20bn cash pile is excluded from the flows because the cash itself is added back, and warehouse-growth capex is charged in full. On that basis even a generous base case of ~7% growth, rising margins and a 20x exit capitalises the business far below today's price, which embeds ~45x earnings and ~50x owner FCF. The finding is that the quality is not in question but the price assumes a perpetual premium exit multiple that the model will not grant.
key_risks_to_valuation: Exit multiple: the model caps terminal value at 20x owner FCF (22x bull); Costco has traded at 40-55x FCF for years, and if that premium persists the model understates value materially.
Membership renewal and fee income are ~half of operating income; a decline in US/Canada renewal from ~90% would hit margins far harder than a sales miss.
Capex intensity: if opening cadence and fulfilment investment keep capex near 2.2% of revenue indefinitely, terminal owner FCF is lower than modelled.
FY0 is an estimate: FY2026 revenue (298.6bn) and the Q4 FY2026 cash flow are not yet in the folder; the FY2026 10-K (due ~Oct 2026) should replace them.
Tariff exposure on imported general merchandise, and e-commerce competition from Amazon and Walmart/Sam's Club.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular close); 52-week range 844.06-1096.50.
data_sources.financials: research/COST/Reports/COST_Metrics.csv (annual FY2008-FY2025) cross-checked against SEC XBRL companyfacts CIK 0000909832 for the FY2025 10-K (filed 2025-10-08) and the Q3 FY2026 10-Q (filed 2026-06-03): balance sheet, diluted shares, SBC, equity-award taxes, interest income, finance leases, taxes paid.
data_sources.qualitative: Company profile in research/COST/info.json; no Analysis JSON exists for COST yet, so scenario axes are drawn from the filings and the business model (membership fees, warehouse openings, e-commerce, international).

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K (SEC XBRL): ShareBasedCompensation cash-flow add-back 860 + taxes paid on net-share settlement of equity awards 393 (financing activities) = 1,253. Costco publishes no combined adjusted-EBITDA SBC figure, so the two lines are summed.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: Q3 FY2026 10-Q weighted-average diluted shares 444.43m (12 weeks to 2026-05-10); basic outstanding 443.51m. Held FLAT because SBC (incl. equity-award taxes) is fully expensed in the flows. Costco is a steady repurchaser (FY2025 $903m, 9M FY2026 $603m), so the flat count is funded, not a modelling convention.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate: 10y UST ~4.3% + beta ~0.8 x 5.0% ERP = ~8.3% cost of equity; debt is <2% of market cap so WACC ~8.0%. Same WACC in every scenario; risk is carried by the scenario paths and weights, not a premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: One treatment: US GAAP ASC 842 operating-lease rent sits inside SG&A, so it is already inside EBITDA and operating-lease liabilities ($2,668m FY2025) are NOT in net debt. Finance-lease liabilities ($1,479m at 2025-08-31, latest disclosed) ARE in total_debt; their amortisation is in D&A and interest is below EBIT, so finance-lease principal is not deducted from the flows.
inputs.nci_treatment: No material non-controlling interest (Taiwan NCI bought out FY2022); none deducted.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build (dcf-methods routing: operating company, US consumer retailer). No prior DCF, no MEMORY entry -> fresh build. FY0 = FY2026E: the fiscal year ended 2026-08-30 but its 10-K/Q4 release is not yet in the folder, so base_revenue is an estimate (FY2025 275,235 x 1.085; H1 FY2026 revenue +8.8% YoY, 9M operating income +12%). Year 1 of the projection is FY2027, which lines up with the Sep-2026 valuation date. Balance sheet is the latest filing (Q3 FY2026 10-Q, 2026-05-10): cash 18,946 + short-term investments 1,050 = 19,996; long-term debt 5,670 (current portion 0) + finance leases 1,479 = 7,149; net cash 12,847. Because the balance sheet predates FY-end, the 16-week Q4 FY2026 owner FCF (~$2-2.5bn before its ~$0.6bn dividend) is in neither the cash nor the flows: a conservative gap of roughly $3-4/share, to be closed when the FY2026 10-K lands. last_fcf is the FY2025 actual (latest audited): 7,837 reported - 1,253 SBC incl. equity-award taxes - 435 interest income = 6,149 (2.23% of revenue). Interest income is stripped because net cash (12.8bn) > 2x the owner-FCF base; 435 is the interest-income component of 'Interest income and other, net' (589 total, remainder FX/other). Working capital is POSITIVE capture: Costco runs negative working capital (payables fund inventory; membership fees are collected in advance), so growth releases cash; FY2023-25 the non-cash-earnings gap in OCF was 7.5-12.5% of the revenue increase, FY2022 negative (inventory build), so 6% base. DATA WARNING for the parser: the Metrics.csv quarter labels are shifted one quarter vs SEC XBRL (CSV 'Q4 2025' revenue 67,307 is XBRL Q1 FY2026; CSV 'Q2 2026' balance sheet is actually 2026-05-10 Q3). Anchors here were read from SEC XBRL companyfacts, not the shifted labels. Ethics screen flagged 'tobacco' (low confidence, incidental merchandise category).

base.ebitda_margin_path_note: EBITDA here is pre-SBC (operating income + D&A + SBC): FY2025 13,669 / 275,235 = 4.97%; FY2026E ~5.0%. Drifts up 35bp over ten years on membership-fee income (Sep-2024 fee rise) and ancillary/advertising mix, with merchandise gross margin reinvested in price.
base.capex_pct_path_note: FY2025 2.0%, FY2026 run-rate ~2.2% (9M capex +20% YoY, ~$6.5bn). Fades to 1.5% as net openings slow; stays above D&A because the terminal still grows 3%.
base.cash_tax_rate_path_note: GAAP effective rate 24.4-25.9% FY2022-25; cash taxes paid 2,917 vs 2,719 expense in FY2025. No carryforward or one-off to ramp.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 15%: no balance-sheet, refinancing or single-customer risk and a 40-year record of renewal rates near 90%, so the downside is slower growth, not impairment. Base 50%: the path continues the FY2022-26 cadence already visible in the filings. Bull 35%: the house default, kept because the bull needs one mechanism Costco has repeated every ~5-6 years (a fee increase) plus sustained international unit growth, both within management's demonstrated control.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
